text: A charge that never reaches the bill is care we gave for free. Here's how charges get on, and who adds what.
This is Maple's visit. The bill builds in the Checkout panel on the right while you work.
Remember this: every charge goes on from this panel. Writing it in the plan doesn't charge it.
To charge something, click the box that says type here to add a charge.
Start typing the item's name.
Pick it from the list.
Maple's plan covers the exam, so it shows as covered, with no charge.
Items the family agreed to on the pre-visit form wait here, under Pre-visit accepts.
Click Accept on the nail trim, and it goes on the bill.
There it is, at Maple's member price.
If the family says no, click Decline. Don't delete it.
Give a reason.
Then click Chart the decline. It goes on the record and the reminder list, so we can offer it again. Don't chart it only takes it off today's bill.
The chews stay here as declined, with the reason. Re-add brings them back if the family changes their mind.
Things the family declined at an earlier visit show here too.
Add to invoice puts one on today's bill if they want it now.
Vaccines need a dose. Medications need a script. Products need a lot. See the vaccine line asking for the dose given?
The panel tells you what's missing, right here.
Who does what? The doctor writes the plan and approves scripts. Techs add charges and record doses. Whoever is with the family takes payment.

The most common mistakes are writing a treatment in the plan and assuming it's charged, and deleting an item the family declined instead of declining it. Remember: every charge goes on from the Checkout panel. The chart and the bill are separate.
